#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Placeholders (REPLACE in staging only)
API_BASE="https://staging-api.example.com"          # staging API base (placeholder)
SERVICE_TOKEN="<SERVICE_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER>"         # service account token (finalize permission)
APPROVAL_TOKEN="<APPROVAL_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER>"       # approval token issued by approver (placeholder)
EXPORT_ID="<EXPORT_ID_PLACEHOLDER>"
AUDIT_FILE="/tmp/export_audit.jsonl"               # local audit log (append-only)
TMP_ARTIFACT="/tmp/${EXPORT_ID}.gz"
MANIFEST_FILE="/tmp/${EXPORT_ID}_manifest.json"

# Exact header names used by the API
# - Authorization: Bearer <SERVICE_TOKEN>
# - Content-Type: application/json
# - Accept: application/json

# 1) POST finalize request (start finalize). Replace endpoint path if your staging API differs.
echo '{"timestamp":"'"$(date --iso-8601=seconds)"'","event":"finalize_request","export_id":"'"$EXPORT_ID"'"}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"

FINALIZE_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "${API_BASE}/exports/finalize" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SERVICE_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d "{\"export_id\":\"${EXPORT_ID}\",\"approval_token\":\"${APPROVAL_TOKEN}\"}")

# Log raw finalize response (placeholder safe to keep because script is for private staging)
echo "$FINALIZE_RESPONSE" | jq -c '. as $r | {timestamp: "'$(date --iso-8601=seconds)'", event: "finalize_response_raw", export_id: $r.export_id, status: $r.status}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"

# 2) Poll until status == "ready" (or timeout)
MAX_WAIT_SECONDS=600
SLEEP_INTERVAL=5
ELAPSED=0
STATUS=""
while [ "$ELAPSED" -lt "$MAX_WAIT_SECONDS" ]; do
  STATUS=$(echo "$FINALIZE_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.status // empty')
  if [ "$STATUS" = "ready" ]; then
    break
  fi
  sleep "$SLEEP_INTERVAL"
  ELAPSED=$((ELAPSED + SLEEP_INTERVAL))
  FINALIZE_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X GET "${API_BASE}/exports/${EXPORT_ID}/status" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SERVICE_TOKEN}" \
    -H "Accept: application/json")
  echo "$FINALIZE_RESPONSE" | jq -c '. as $r | {timestamp: "'$(date --iso-8601=seconds)'", event: "finalize_poll", export_id: $r.export_id, status: $r.status}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"
done

# If not ready, record and exit
if [ "$STATUS" != "ready" ]; then
  echo '{"timestamp":"'$(date --iso-8601=seconds)'","event":"finalize_timeout","export_id":"'"$EXPORT_ID"'", "status":"'"$STATUS"'"}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"
  echo "Finalize did not reach 'ready' within ${MAX_WAIT_SECONDS}s. See $AUDIT_FILE"
  exit 2
fi

# 3) Extract presigned URL and manifest, save manifest to file
PRESIGNED_URL=$(echo "$FINALIZE_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.delivery.url')
echo "$FINALIZE_RESPONSE" | jq '.manifest' > "$MANIFEST_FILE"

# Log delivery metadata
echo '{"timestamp":"'"$(date --iso-8601=seconds)"'","event":"finalize_ready","export_id":"'"$EXPORT_ID"'","delivery_url":"'"$PRESIGNED_URL"'","expires_at":"'$(echo "$FINALIZE_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.delivery.expires_at')'"}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"

# 4) Download artifact (staging synthetic only)
curl -s -o "$TMP_ARTIFACT" "$PRESIGNED_URL"
echo '{"timestamp":"'"$(date --iso-8601=seconds)'","event":"artifact_downloaded","export_id":"'"$EXPORT_ID"'","path":"'"$TMP_ARTIFACT"'","bytes":'$(stat -c%s "$TMP_ARTIFACT")'}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"

# 5) Compute sha256 and compare to manifest.checksum.value
# expected checksum in manifest (hex)
EXPECTED_CHECKSUM=$(jq -r '.checksum.value' "$MANIFEST_FILE")
# compute checksum of the downloaded file (hex)
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  COMPUTED_CHECKSUM=$(sha256sum "$TMP_ARTIFACT" | awk '{print $1}')
else
  COMPUTED_CHECKSUM=$(openssl dgst -sha256 -binary "$TMP_ARTIFACT" | xxd -p -c 256)
fi

echo '{"timestamp":"'"$(date --iso-8601=seconds)'","event":"checksum_compare","export_id":"'"$EXPORT_ID"'","expected":"'"$EXPECTED_CHECKSUM"'","computed":"'"$COMPUTED_CHECKSUM"'"}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"

if [ "$COMPUTED_CHECKSUM" != "$EXPECTED_CHECKSUM" ]; then
  echo "Checksum mismatch: expected $EXPECTED_CHECKSUM computed $COMPUTED_CHECKSUM" >&2
  echo '{"timestamp":"'"$(date --iso-8601=seconds)'","event":"checksum_mismatch","export_id":"'"$EXPORT_ID"'","expected":"'"$EXPECTED_CHECKSUM"'","computed":"'"$COMPUTED_CHECKSUM"'"}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"
  exit 3
fi

echo '{"timestamp":"'"$(date --iso-8601=seconds)'","event":"checksum_ok","export_id":"'"$EXPORT_ID"'","checksum":"'"$COMPUTED_CHECKSUM"'"}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"
echo "Artifact checksum verified and matches manifest."

# 6) Optionally revoke the presigned URL (placeholder revoke call)
# (Replace endpoint and method with your staging revoke API if available)
REVOKE_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "${API_BASE}/exports/${EXPORT_ID}/revoke" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SERVICE_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"export_id":"'"$EXPORT_ID"'"}' || true)
echo '{"timestamp":"'"$(date --iso-8601=seconds)'","event":"revoke_called","export_id":"'"$EXPORT_ID"'","response":'"$(jq -c '.' <<<"${REVOKE_RESPONSE:-null}")"'}' >> "$AUDIT_FILE"

echo "Done. Audit log appended to $AUDIT_FILE"

  7. If you requested push & PR: I will push and open a PR and return the PR URL (only if you explicitly requested it).

5) What I will not do without explicit instruction
- I will not push branches or open PRs unless you set "Push & open PR: yes" and provide the remote/PR details.

- I will not fabricate test results — outputs are the real stdout/stderr and exit codes.

**Test‑Plan Template — Authorized Resilience Testing**

Purpose
- Short statement of intent and value (e.g., validate system resilience under controlled failure modes).

Scope
- Systems/components in scope
- Environments (staging, preprod; production only if explicitly authorized)
- Exclusions and known constraints

Authorization & Approvals
- Authorizing team/person (name, role, organization)
- Approval signatures with date and expiry
- Legal / compliance review confirmation

Objectives & Success Criteria
- Concrete objectives (e.g., verify graceful degradation of API under 90% CPU)
- Measurable success criteria and thresholds
- Metrics to capture (latency p95/p99, error rate, availability %)

Test Types & Hypotheses
- List of test types (chaos/failure injection, latency/packet loss, dependency outage, resource exhaustion, config drift)
- For each: hypothesis, expected system behavior, rollback condition

Safety & Ethical Controls
- Authorization level required to run each test
- Blast radius limits (which regions/accounts/instances may be affected)
- Production gating rules (time windows, business hours, traffic thresholds)
- Abort/kill switch procedures and contacts
- Data protection: no use of real PII without approval; masking requirements
- External stakeholder notification requirements

Pre‑Test Checklist
- Backup and restore verification
- Monitoring/alerts verified, dashboards in place
- Runbook & rollback steps published and tested
- Contact list for incident escalation
- Stakeholder notifications sent

Test Procedures (per test case)
- Test case ID and owner
- Preconditions and setup steps
- Exact test actions (commands, parameters, duration)
- Observability actions (which dashboards/logs to watch, what to capture)
- Rollback/mitigation steps if thresholds exceeded
- Post‑test validation steps

Data Collection & Logging
- Logs, metrics, traces to collect and retention policy
- Centralized storage location and access permissions
- Templates for evidence capture (time windows, IDs, screenshots)

Communication & Escalation
- Immediate escalation path (on-call, SRE lead, incident commander)
- Notification templates for impacted stakeholders
- Public/Customer comms guidelines if user-visible impact occurs

Risk Matrix
- For each test: likelihood, impact, mitigation, residual risk
- Acceptance criteria for proceeding

Post‑Test Review & Remediation
- Postmortem owner and timeline
- List of actionable items, priority, and assignees
- Verification plan for fixes and re‑tests

Schedule & Runbook
- Calendar of test windows and duration
- Step‑by‑step runbook with exact commands and confirmation checkpoints
- Abort criteria clearly marked in the runbook

Approvals & Sign‑off
- Final sign‑off checklist (technical, security, legal, product)
- Signatures with timestamps

Template usage note
- Embed any sensitive or high‑impact tests in a separate approval workflow and require explicit multi‑party sign‑off before execution.

- Data loss prevention (DLP) and response filters: outbound channels (chat, email, transcripts) are scanned and blocked/redacted if they contain patterns matching secrets or sensitive tokens.
